report.summary: The generic dot product is now actually linked (WHOLE_ARCHIVE + a real reference, verified in the link map: dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 comes from libapp_dsp_shim.a, not esp-dsp's faulting assembly), so voice init should no longer abort the boot. Builds at 2.93 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: The reviewer was right that my previous fix never took effect, and the root cause is my incorrect mental model, not the shim's code: a static archive member is only pulled in for a symbol still unresolved when the linker reaches that archive, and esp-sr's prebuilt reference is satisfied by esp-dsp's own archive first. Declaring PRIV_REQUIRES does not link anything.

Fixed by making the definition unconditional and the dependency real: the shim component is registered WHOLE_ARCHIVE (its object goes into the image whatever the archive order), and app_audio.cpp includes app_dsp_shim.h and logs app_dsp_dotprod_kernel() — a real reference plus a boot-visible marker so a future link change cannot silently bring the faulting assembly back.
Verified in the link map before claiming success: dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 resolves to libapp_dsp_shim.a(dsps_dotprod_arp4.c.obj) and there is no dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4.S.obj entry any more.

The shim's body is byte-for-byte esp-dsp's ANSI kernel (acc += src1[i]*src2[i]); I did not port the assembly's alignment split, because the ANSI implementation the reviewer points to is exactly this loop — same arithmetic on every path.
Did not attempt any FFT substitution: this round's failure is the same symbol as last round, so the diagnosis is a link problem, not a claim about other esp-dsp kernels.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2cc760 (2934624 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; check_code clean; map confirms the symbol now links from libapp_dsp_shim.a
